parsed.explanation: Combined regime: locally protective DC-like jurisdiction with no own bathroom ban and local anti-discrimination law, but national law applies directly. Federal binary-sex order, passport-marker restriction, entry discrepancy cable, government-facility exclusion, Congress-attached bathroom ban, and documented federal custody abuse create recurring tier-1 exposures for an outed visitor. Courts challenge some orders, but no documented effective remedy for federal facilities, entry screening, or custody. Local hotels/services may be welcoming; federal touchpoints dominate after outing.

entry_documents.exposure: Foreign ministry stopped X-marker passports; existing X valid to expiry, new only M/F. Cable: document discrepancy causing reasonable doubt requires refusal and more evidence; suspected wilful misrepresentation may be considered for permanent fraud ineligibility, not automatic. Passports confiscated/blocked reported.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration; fraud finding requires all elements and limited waivers; passport policy challenged in courts.
entry_documents.interaction: A marker/presentation discrepancy at entry can escalate from refusal to fraud consideration, detention, and birth-sex custody, bypassing local protections.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections from 2026 adopted conversion-therapy model: short hair, hormone removal, psychiatric substitution; care denial reported. Immigration custody: trans men reported forced labour, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. No jurisdiction-specific custody conditions or placement protocol provided.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any entry, facility-trespass, or protest arrest can lead into federal custody where documented abuse and care removal apply, despite local law.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity. This jurisdiction has no own ban, but Congress attached a facilities restriction; activists protesting it at federal building were arrested 5 Dec 2024. Scope unspecified.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Locally elected legislature has not enacted its own ban; jurisdiction listed low-risk July 2026, but Congress can override local protections.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Private/local venues may admit by identity, while federal buildings common in this seat are governed by national restriction that local council cannot repeal.

care_services.exposure: Federal custody removes hormone medication. National measures restrict gender-affirming care for minors and propose barring public insurance for under-18 care; emergency/visitor adult care practice not documented.
care_services.protection: Not documented for visitors. Several national orders blocked/enjoined, status unresolved at travel.
care_services.interaction: Emergency care may be ordinary locally, but if detained, medication can be withdrawn under federal custody policy.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National policy defines sex as binary at birth, removes gender-identity materials, directs scrutiny of schools, and 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritizes radically pro-transgender violent groups. Officials frame inclusion as threat to women/fairness in facilities/sports contexts.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 22 states plus capital district outlaw gender-identity discrimination. Challenges to several orders are pending.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing supports federal facility/entry enforcement; street-level local hostility and police response for visitors are not documented.

minors_guardians.exposure: Adult travelling with a trans minor faces national hostile regime: 27 jurisdictions ban minor gender-affirming care, federal order directs criminal investigation of teachers facilitating social transition, DOJ subpoenaed hospitals for under-19 records. Visitor-specific application not documented.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented. No visitor shield for travelling families documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor needing care, school enrolment, or facilities could trigger federal/state scrutiny; a non-trans minor travelling with trans adult mainly faces adult's exposures.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No jurisdiction-specific police practice, street violence rate, or visitor assault record documented. National polling shows majority support birth-sex documents, indicating social hostility risk, but not visitor violence prevalence.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Local anti-discrimination law and national hate-crime law exist; low-risk legal assessment July 2026. Enforcement outcomes not documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local police may be more protective than federal actors, but federal law-enforcement and custody exposure remains if federal encounter escalates.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Scope/enforcement of Congress-attached bathroom ban, local custody, local hate-crime enforcement, and visitor emergency care are deliberately not documented. Low-risk ranking method not described.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties suits, injunctions on several orders, and legal-aid passport FAQ provide partial recourse; no documented remedy changing federal facility/custody practice.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unresolved litigation means exposure depends on measures in effect at travel; local reputation is not durable against national override.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: universal birth-sex facility exclusion in public buildings with courts not yet providing effective relief, despite polite private interactions. Here federal facilities and Congress-attached ban create same tier-1 exposure, plus entry and custody risks.

Slightly lower: 0.45-A has one unremedied bathroom rule but no documented entry fraud risk or federal custody abuse. This dossier stacks federal facility, passport/entry, and custody exposures, while local protections keep it above 0.35.

Higher risk than 0.65-A: that anchor has no facility ban, working refunds/training, and convictions for attackers. Here bathroom exclusion is legally imposed federally, remedies are litigated rather than demonstrated, and custody abuse is documented, so working protection is absent.

parsed.synthesis: The operative interaction is local welcome versus federal control. Hotels and local services likely benefit from no local ban and local anti-discrimination law, but the traveller cannot avoid federal buildings, federal passports/entry screening, federal police, or federal custody in the national seat. Once outed at a federal touchpoint, birth-sex facility rules, possible entry refusal/fraud consideration, protest/trespass arrest risk, and documented custody abuse follow. Pending lawsuits and injunctions do not document a working remedy for those exposures, and Congress can override local protections without local change.
